label: input "e" at original position 4
explanation: Fires only on the original-phase input token "e", and almost entirely when it is the 5th original token (t=4). On that predicate it fires at nearly every such step (precision ~1.0) with strong activation, and this accounts for 94% of activation mass. Weak spillover activations (lowest quartile, about 6% of mass) occur on "e" at t=3 or t=5. Never fires on other tokens, on the delimiter, or during the copy phase. Magnitude is about the same across L; first occurrences of e give somewhat higher rates. A position-specific token detector for e@4.

issues: Wrong secondary claim: 'firing rate is higher when this is the first e' does not hold. On dev, e at t=4 with in_first==1 has precision 0.9997 and with in_first==0 has precision 0.9994, so it fires about 100% of the time either way. The mass-to-count ratio is slightly higher for repeated e (0.134/0.101=1.32 vs 0.802/0.677=1.19), so repeated e if anything activates a bit more strongly. This sentence should be removed from the explanation; it does not affect the label or predicate.

Core claims hold. Test: P=0.9998, R=0.777, F1=0.874, mass recall 0.935. Quartile coverage is [0.115, 0.993, 1.0, 1.0]. There is 0 activation on the delimiter step, in the copy phase, or on any token other than e. All activations fall at t in {3,4,5}. The L=4 share (0.006) comes entirely from e at t=3, which is consistent with the explanation.

Missed activations (test split, 3924 steps, 6.5% of mass) are weak firings on e at t=3 (P=0.156) and t=5 (P=0.131). Splitting them by seen(e), in_count, digit or vowel previous token, n_digits, or L gave no subset with precision above about 0.23, so they look like diffuse positional bleed rather than a systematic class.
False positives on the test split: only 3 steps (e at t=4 inactive). This is scattered noise.
